text: Thursday morning, Geum marches into the Association's Busan branch, ladle first.
Her report is a ladle slammed on the branch chief's desk. He just lifts his tea out of the way.
Pim salutes and gives evidence. Branch Chief Yang has never taken a statement from a husk.
Yang looks at the red pin on his map. Geum's word is proof enough.
He reaches for the phone, and the screen on the wall lights up.
Deputy Director Hwang, calling from Seoul, already knows exactly who is in the room.
It's the press conference smile again: Jaeha is unreliable, Kanghan has the lid, nobody evacuates.
Slowly, Yang puts the receiver back.
As Hwang smooths his lapel, the underside flips up for an instant: a small silver hexagon.
Jaeha first spotted that pin on a paused press conference. It's still there.
Out the window, a black crane barge sits right over the lid. Hwang's goodbye sounds like a threat.
Pim winces. Out there, the barge makes a racket only he can hear.
Yang apologises on the steps: Seoul holds his purse strings. Geum needs nobody's permission. Then Jaeha's phone buzzes.
Han Sora, inviting him to a rooftop pool at eleven. Baek wanted him to come to them.
So Jaeha walks into a luxury hotel in a borrowed tracksuit, with a goblin.
Sora lounges by the pool in a black swimsuit, cocktail in hand, completely at ease. She compliments the tracksuit.
Jaeha suddenly finds the sky very interesting. Nib is unimpressed.
Baek's offer: work for Kanghan, name the price. They've done their homework. The list starts with Seoa.
Her tablet shows Kanghan's anchors: harpoons on huge chains, each link stamped with a mark.
Jaeha holds up his own link, saved from the chains on Nib's commander. Same mark.
The blush is gone. Kanghan doesn't want to seal the sea, Jaeha says. It wants a second farm.
Sora doesn't deny it. She sips and plays Baek's favourite card: the hospitals.
Jaeha stands. His answer for Baek is short.
Sora flicks her sunglasses down. Baek predicted the no, and what comes after it.
On the way out, Nib steals the little umbrella from her drink.
And Sora actually laughs out loud.
At one o'clock, a crowd gathers on the beach round a white drone.
Lyra wades out of the sea in a river-blue bikini and poses for the drone. Applause was always clause one.
Bomi has come down from Seoul for her Busan stream after all. Geum banned cameras in the tent, not the beach.
Four hundred thousand are watching, and the chat wants to know about the fluffy guy.
Under Borro's umbrella, Jaeha develops a sudden passion for clouds. Pim notices. Jaeha defends the cloud.
Tourists mistake Pim for a mascot. His rank is no help here either.
Then two smiling people with hexagon pins bring Lyra a glossy folder. Kanghan wants a new face.
Her face on a billboard beside the hexagon, and a contract, pen attached.
Applause and money: two of her three terms when she joined. Her fingers drift toward the pen.
She glances at Jaeha, who shrugs and leaves it to her. He's learned to let his summons choose.
Lyra hands the pen back, dazzling. She's already under contract, to the worst businessman she knows.
Jaeha goes red to the ears.
On the stream, over a million people watch her turn down Kanghan.
Then a line of perfect white husks marches down the beach, carrying luggage.
Moon Ahin crosses the sand in white under Saebyeok's parasol, like she owns the beach. She was passing, of course.
Lyra and Moon Ahin square up, a little too close. Lyra has the height. Moon Ahin has the attitude.
Then the half-smile drops. Kanghan's own papers make Busan another farm, like the one they barely escaped. She's going to inspect it.
So the heir of Kanghan speeds out to the barge, holding her hat on.
Her own family's engineers block the gangway, troopers behind them. Her uncle saw this coming too.
Her hand tightens on her baton. Saebyeok steps in front of her.
She turns away, white with anger. Her message for her uncle is very short.
Back on the beach, the two women share a lounger back to back. Neither budges.
The barge told her nothing. Jaeha knows someone who hears everything.
At five, they gather at the end of the breakwater, the barge far out on a golden sea.
Jaeha asks if radio is within Pim's range. Pim is deeply offended by the question.
His wings open in field form, and his signal reaches out toward the barge.
Through LINK, Jaeha catches the barge's radio. Kanghan goes into the lid first thing tomorrow.
Pim relays it in a flat radio voice. They want their hooks in first.
Someone asks the only sensible question. Baek has already answered it: more chains.
Geum's steel arm twitches hard. The last time that thing came up, it took her real one.
Geum has guarded that lid for ten years. Kanghan would crack it to start a farm, and Moon Ahin knows her uncle would.
Jaeha writes it down: Friday at six. The Friday he promised Seoa dinner.
Pim's wings fold round him. For once, the signal keeper wishes he'd heard less.
Out at sea, the barge's floodlights snap on. The drills hang ready, and under the hull, the violet spreads.
